prerequisites: Basic knowledge of manufacturing processes is expected for the Manufacturing Technology Lab.

learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire basic knowledge about the essential manufacturing processes for the production of products from various materials with different qualities and in different quantities. They gain practical experience through practice in the independent production of workpieces using forging, bending, laser cutting, turning, milling, drilling, grinding, and welding processes on conventional machines and NC machines, and learn how to handle machines and equipment responsibly.
Describe essential manufacturing processes for different materials, qualities, and quantities.
Designate manufacturing processes according to DIN 8580.
Apply suitable processes for given product requirements.
Plan process chains for the production of typical workpieces.
Perform forging, bending, laser cutting, turning, milling, drilling, grinding, and welding on conventional machines and NC machines.
Enter NC parameters into controls and use processing steps according to specifications.
Execute safety and operating instructions on machines.
Identify typical defects and dimensional deviations through suitable tests.
Summarize results of dimensional and surface inspections.
Apply joining processes and rapid prototyping using practical examples.
Present safety instructions and work instructions in a team.
Identify risks, priorities, and dependencies in the manufacturing process.
Fill out inspection and production protocols according to standards.
Plan work and time schedules for manufacturing orders.
Work on tasks in shift and team work.
Constructively discuss feedback on dimensional and quality deviations.
Summarize project results and learning experiences concisely.

syllabus_topics: Primary shaping with metallic materials from the liquid state (casting with lost molds, casting with permanent molds, casting of semi-finished products)
Primary shaping with thermoplastics (injection molding, extrusion)
Machining with geometrically defined cutting edge (broaching, turning, drilling, milling, threading, reaming)
Machining with geometrically undefined cutting edge (grinding, honing, lapping)
teaching_methods: Lectures on manufacturing processes (supported by video technology)
Performing simple calculation examples (estimation of power requirements, main time calculation)
Independent production of a simple product using different manufacturing processes (practice of learned material)

assessment_methods.method: Written examination with calculation examples and theory questions

assessment_rules: The applied teaching and learning methods, as well as the examination modalities, are to be specified in the information system for studies and teaching for each course before the start of the semester.
